Rashi on Eruvin 53b:10:1.english: (Or) Let [us] remove after its fellow from it - We will remove the stopper of the other barrel and pour more.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:10:2.english: And let the ladle float in the jug - Let the ladle float in the jug with ample room.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:10:3.hebrew: כאילפא בימא - כאניה הצפה בים. תתקפי — כמו אקפו ידייכו בחגיגה (דף טז:), וכמו קפא תהומא דסוכה (דף נג.) — צף התהום ועלה:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:10:3.english: Like a ship in the sea - Like a ship floating on the sea. [The word] titkafei [let it float] is like “akpu yadaikhu” [keep your hands afloat] in Chagigah (16b), and like “kafa tehoma” in Sukkah (53a) — the deep floated and rose.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:11:1.english: In enigmatic language - So that others would not understand.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:11:2.hebrew: שור משפט - תרדין — תור דין: שור — תור, משפט — דין:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:11:2.english: An ox [in] judgment - Beets, [namely] tor din: "ox" [in Aramaic is] tor, [and] "judgment" [is] din.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:11:3.english: On a poor mountain - [Mountain is] har, [and] poor [is] dal — [yielding] chardal [mustard].

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:12:1.english: Inquiring about an inn - [He was] asking passersby concerning an innkeeper.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:12:2.hebrew: גבר פום דין חי - אוש פי זו חי — אוש כמו איש, פום כמו פי, דין כמו זה:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:12:2.english: “A man, [the] mouth of this [one is] raw” - [This forms the phrase] osh-pi-zu-ḥai [alluding to ushpiza, an inn]: “Osh” is like ish [“man”, translating gevar]; “pum” [“mouth of”] is like pi; “dein” [“this”] is like zeh [i.e., zu].

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:12:3.hebrew: מה זו טובה יש - כלומר, כמה טוב לו:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:12:3.english: What is this good that there is - That is to say: How well is he doing?

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:13:1.hebrew: אתריגו לפחמין ארקיעו לזהבין - הבעירו את הפחמין להיות אדומין כאתרוג, שישטחו גחלים הלוחשות על פי הכירה להתחמם כנגדן:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:13:1.english: Make the coals like an etrog; spread out the golden ones - Kindle the coals so that they become red like an etrog, [and] that they should spread glowing coals over the opening of the stove to warm themselves by them.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:13:2.english: Beat - Spread [them] out like a firmament:

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:13:3.english: The golden ones - Glowing coals, red like gold.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:13:4.english: Speakers in the dark - Roosters, which announce the times of the night.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:1.hebrew: הצפיננו - הראנו, לשון ”צופיה הליכות ביתה“ (משלי לא):
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:1.english: Show us - [Means] show us; an expression [similar to]: “She watches over [tzofiyyah] the ways of her household” (Proverbs 31:27).

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:2.hebrew: צפון - הוה מתחבא, דלא היו יודעים התלמידים להיכן היה, והיו שואלים ממנו:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:2.english: Hidden - He was hiding, as the students did not know where he was, and they were asking him.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:3.hebrew: עלץ בנערה אהרונית אחרונית עירנית והנעירתו - שמח הלילה בנערה אהרונית, ועכשיו הוא ישן:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:3.english: He rejoiced with an Aharonic, latter, lively girl, and she kept him awake - He rejoiced during the night with an Aharonic girl, and now he is sleeping:

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:4.hebrew: עירנית - בעלת חן וחריפה, כאדם ער. והנעירתו — לא היה יכול לישון:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:14:4.english: Lively - Charming and sharp-witted, like an alert person. And "she kept him awake" — he was not able to sleep.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:15:1.hebrew: אמרי לה אשה - אהרונית — בת כהן. אחרונית — מתה אשתו ראשונה, וזו אחרונה:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:15:1.english: Some say [it refers to] a woman - “Aharonic” — a daughter of a priest. “Latter” — his first wife had died, and this [one is] a latter [wife].

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:16:1.hebrew: מסכתא - אהרונית — מסדר קדשים, עבודת אהרן. אחרונית — סיים אחרת והתחיל בזו. עירנית — עמוקה וחמורה, ומעוררת לומדיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:16:1.english: A tractate - “Aharonic” — from the order of Kodashim, [which deals with] the service of Aaron. “Latter” — he finished another [tractate] and began this one. “Lively” — [it is] deep and difficult, and awakens its students.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:17:1.hebrew: נתיעץ במכתיר - נטל רשות מנשיא. מכתיר — ע"ש שנותן רשות לסמוך ולקרותו רבי, ומאז והלאה הוא כשר להיות מוכתר ליקרא רבי, מומחה לרבים, ואם טעה — לא ישלם:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:17:1.english: He took counsel with the one who crowns - He received authorization from the Nasi. [He is called] “the one who crowns” because he gives authorization to ordain [a scholar] and to call him Rabbi; and from then on, he is qualified to be crowned, to be called Rabbi, [as] an expert for the public, and if he erred, he does not pay [restitution].

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:17:2.english: And went south - And headed south; he went to the South.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:17:3.hebrew: למפיבושת - לפני זקני דרום, שהן חכמים מאד. ע"ש שהיה מפיבשת אדם גדול, קרי להו הכי:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:17:3.english: To Mephibosheth - Before the Elders of the South, who are very wise. Because Mephibosheth was a great man, he called them this.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:18:1.english: No person defeated me - In words [i.e., in debate].

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:18:2.hebrew: הקדיחתו - שרפתו, כמו ”כי אש קדחה“ (דברים ל״ב:כ״ב) — כלומר, נתנה בו מלח יותר מדאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:18:2.english: She burned it - She burned it, as in: “For a fire is kindled” (Deuteronomy 32:22) — that is to say, she put too much salt into it.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:1:1.english: He did them mischief - He did not merit to rule in accordance with the halakhah.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:20:1.hebrew: אין משיירין פאה באילפס - כשהשמש מערה מן האילפס לתוך הקערה, אין דרך להניח באילפס כלום לצורכו. אבל כל אחד מניח פאה בקערה ומחזירה לשמש, והוא מאכל שמש:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:20:1.english: One does not leave a remainder in the pot - When the server pours from the pot into the plate, it is not customary to leave anything in the pot for his needs. Rather, each person leaves a remainder on the plate and returns it to the server, and that is the server's food.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:22:1.english: A crossroads - A road branches this way and that.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:22:2.english: Long - In that it lengthens the way.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:22:3.english: And short - In that it brings [one] out to an alleyway of the city [that is] clear to enter.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:2:1.english: For that sin - The sin of Nov, the city of priests.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:2:2.hebrew: אתה ובניך עמי - שמואל קאמר לשאול, כשהעלהו על ידי בעלת אוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:2:2.english: You and your sons [will be] with me - Samuel said [this] to Saul when he raised him up by means of the necromancer.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:3:1.hebrew: אכוזו תנן או עכוזו - בבכורות (דף מ.) גבי מומין תנן: שאין לו אלא ביצה אחת — הרי זה מום; רבי עקיבא אומר: מושיבין אותו על עכוזו וממעך, אם יש ביצה אחרת — סופה לצאת. אכוזו — עגבותיו, וכן עכוזו:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:3:1.english: Did we learn akkuzo [with an alef] or akkuzo [with an ayin] - In Bekhorot (40a), regarding blemishes, we learned [in the Mishnah]: “[An animal] that has only one testicle, this is a blemish. Rabbi Akiva says: One sits it on its hindquarters and presses; if there is another testicle, it will eventually emerge.” Akkuzo [means] its hindquarters, and likewise akkuzo [has the same meaning].

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:3:2.english: They would know - [That is,] they would know.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:5:1.english: Like beets on the ground - It was greenish, like the color of the greenery of the earth.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:6:1.hebrew: אמר למאן - מדבר בשפה רפה, ולא פירש האות, ואינו ניכר אם עמר, אם חמר, אם אימר:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:6:1.english: Who has amar? - [He was] speaking with soft pronunciation and did not articulate the letter [clearly], and it was not discernible whether [he meant] wool [ʿamar], whether [a donkey or wine, ḥamar], [or] whether a lamb [imar].

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:6:2.english: Wool to wear - To make garments.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:6:3.english: A lamb to be slaughtered - A lamb to slaughter.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:7:1.hebrew: תא דאוכליך חלבא - היתה רוצה לומר: ״בואי ואוכליך חלב״, ואינה מפרשת לחתוך תיבות זו מזו ולהשמיע כל תיבה ותיבה, ומצטרפות שתי תיבות כאחת [ומגמגמת התיבות ואומרת: ״תאכליך לביא״]. ואומרת נמי ״שלוכתי״ בכ"ף, והיתה רוצה לומר ״שלובתי״ בב', כמו ״משולבות״ — כלומר, חברתי:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:7:1.english: Come, that I may feed you milk - She wanted to say: “Come, and I will feed you milk,” but she did not articulate [clearly enough] to separate the words from one another and enunciate each and every word, so two words combined into one [and she muddled the words and said: “May a lioness eat you”]. And she also said “shelukhati” with a kaf, when she wanted to say “sheluvati” with a beit, like “joined” [meshulavot] — that is to say, my companion.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:7:2.hebrew: תוכליך לביא - קללה משמע, שתאכלך לביא:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:7:2.english: May a lioness eat you - It implies a curse, that a lioness should eat you.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:1.hebrew: מרי כירי - ורוצה לומר קירי, והוא אדון; ואמרה כירי, והוא עבד:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:1.english: Mari kiri - And [she] meant to say kiri [with a kuf], which is "master," but she said kiri [with a kaf], which is "servant."

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:2.hebrew: תפלא הות לי - רוצה לומר: ״טבלא הות לי״, ואמרה ״תפלא״ — והיא קורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:2.english: I had a tafla - [She] meant to say: "I had a tavla [a board]," but she said "tafla" — and that is a beam.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:3.hebrew: וגנבוך מין - רוצה לומר: ״גנבוה ממני״, ואמרה: ״גנבוך מין״, דמשמע שגנבו את הדיין:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:3.english: And they stole you from me - [She] meant to say: “They stole it from me,” but she said: “They stole you from me,” which implies that they stole the judge.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:4.hebrew: וכדו הות דכי שדרו לך עילויה לא מטיין כרעיך אארעא - גדולה היתה כ"כ, שאם מותחין אותך עליה לא היו רגליך נוגעות בארץ. והרי שטויות הרבה: ״וכדו״ משמע עכשיו, ובעיא לומר ״וכדן הות״; ועוד, שהיתה מזכרת תלייה בדיין, ואומרת: ״אם תולין אותך עליה״, כו':
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:8:4.english: And it was so, that when they would hang you upon it, your feet would not reach the ground - [She meant that] it was so large that if they were to stretch you out upon it, your feet would not touch the ground. And behold, [there is] much foolishness [in her words]: “Ukhdu” implies “now,” whereas she needed to say “ukhedan havat” [“and such it was”]; and furthermore, that she mentioned hanging in reference to the judge, saying: “If they hang you upon it...” etc.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:9:1.english: The ladle - The name of a vessel with which one draws wine from the cask and fills the cups.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:9:2.hebrew: נקפת בכד - מנקפת בחבית, כלומר: כבר כלה היין, והכלי נוגע בתחתית החבית:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:9:2.english: Knocking against the jug - Knocks against the cask; that is to say, the wine has already run out, [and the ladle] touches the bottom of the cask.

Rashi on Eruvin 53b:9:3.hebrew: ידאון נישריא לקיניהון - ילכו תלמידים לבתיהם, כלומר, יפסקו סעודתן [שאין עוד יין]:
Rashi on Eruvin 53b:9:3.english: Let the eagles fly to their nests - Let the students go to their homes; that is to say, let them end their meal [for there is no more wine].

Tosafot on Eruvin 53b:12:1.hebrew: גבר פום דין חי - פי' רבינו חננאל: אושפיזכנא. תרגום איש — גבר, ופי — פום, זה — דין, נא — חי; "אל תאכלו ממנו נא" מתרגמינן "כד חי" (שמות י״ב:ט׳):
Tosafot on Eruvin 53b:12:1.english: "Man, mouth, this, raw" - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [This alludes to an] ushpizkhana [an innkeeper]. The [Aramaic] translation of ish [man] is gvar; and [of] pi [mouth] is pum; [of] zeh [this] is din; [and of] na [raw] is chai — [as in the verse,] "Do not eat of it raw [na]" (Exodus 12:9), which we translate [in the Targum as] "when raw [kad chai]".

Tosafot on Eruvin 53b:20:1.hebrew: משיירין פיאה בקערה ואין משיירין פיאה באילפס - בפרק בן עזאי קתני: "משיירין פיאה במעשה קדירה, ואין משיירין פיאה במעשה אילפס". פירוש: במעשה קדירה נראה כרעבתן אם אינו משייר, אבל במעשה אילפס אינו נראה כרעבתן אם אינו משייר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 53b:20:1.english: One leaves a remainder on the plate, but one does not leave a remainder in the pot [ilpas] - In the chapter of Ben Azzai, [the baraita] teaches: "One leaves a remainder in [the case of] a pot dish, but one does not leave a remainder in [the case of] a stew-pot [ilpas] dish." Explanation: In [the case of] a pot dish, he appears like a glutton if he does not leave [a remainder], but in [the case of] a stew-pot dish, he does not appear like a glutton if he does not leave [a remainder].

Tosafot on Eruvin 53b:9:1.hebrew: עלת נקפת בכד - כלי שדולין בו יין מן הכד. והא דאמר בפרק כל כתבי (שבת דף קיט.) גבי רב יוסף מוקר שבי, ובפרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלג:) גבי יוסף בן יועזר: "זבני בתליסר עיליתא דדינרי" — מפרש ר"ת דעיליתא הוא כלי, כמו עלת דהכא; ולא כמו שפי' בקונט' שם: עליות, וגוזמא קאמר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 53b:9:1.english: "The ladle is knocking against the jug" - [Olat is] a vessel with which one draws wine from the jug. And that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Kol Kitvei (Shabbat 119a) regarding Rav Yosef Mokir Shabbat, and in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 133b) regarding Yosef ben Yoezer: "[He] sold [it] for thirteen ilitah of dinars" — Rabbeinu Tam explains that an ilitah is a vessel, like olat here, and not as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres there: [that it means] attics [aliyyot], and [the Gemara] was speaking hyperbolically.
